s: the guava-and-cheese pastry that made this Roma bakery a citywide obsession
w: Chef Elena Reygadas's bakery, an offshoot of her restaurant Rosetta, built its citywide reputation on a single pastry: the guava roll, a croissant-style dough wrapped around cream cheese custard and tart guava jam. Small enough that seats at the bar or streetside tables fill fast, with a queue down the block a near-permanent fixture.
_facts: Located at Colima 179, Roma Norte, Cuauhtémoc, Mexico City
Founded by chef Elena Reygadas as an extension of her restaurant Rosetta
Best known for its guava roll, blending Mexican and French pastry techniques
Regularly draws long queues, especially on weekends

s: a 150-year-old sweets shop on Avenida 5 de Mayo
w: A traditional Mexican dulcería founded in 1874 by brothers Alfredo and Luis Guízar de Arias, still trading on Avenida 5 de Mayo in the historic centre. Glass cases hold camotes, jamoncillos, ates and other candied fruit and milk sweets largely unchanged in over a century and a half -- one of the oldest continuously operating sweet shops in the city.
_facts: Located at Avenida 5 de Mayo 39, Centro Histórico, Mexico City
Founded in 1874 by brothers Alfredo and Luis Guízar de Arias
Specialises in traditional Mexican candied sweets: camotes, jamoncillos, ates and more
One of the oldest sweets shops in Mexico City

s: a quiet corner café in Condesa built for lingering, not rushing
w: A stylish, understated café on a Condesa corner, indoor and outdoor seating built for staying a while over a flat white and an almond pain au chocolat rather than grabbing a cup and moving on. One of the calmer, less shouted-about entries in the neighbourhood's dense coffee scene.
_facts: Located at Fernando Montes de Oca 55, Condesa, Cuauhtémoc, Mexico City
Known for flat whites and pastries including almond pain au chocolat
Has both indoor and outdoor seating

s: a Parque México patisserie known for its raspberry kouign amann
w: A patisserie facing Parque México in Hipódromo-Condesa, its raspberry kouign amann -- deeply caramelised at the edges, tightly laminated -- among the most talked-about pastries in the neighbourhood. Bread, croissants and coffee round out a menu built for a park-facing breakfast.
_facts: Located at Plaza Popocatépetl 35, Hipódromo, Condesa, Mexico City, facing Parque México
Known especially for its raspberry kouign amann
Also serves bread, croissants, coffee and breakfast
